sources.note: AIGA Eye on Design: names Turntable.fm, SoundCloud, Bandcamp around 2010-2011; pink/teal gradients, Greek sculptures, palm trees, Word Art, full-width text, VHS graininess, Floral Shoppe cover described.

daisyUI: palette, busts, grids, checker floors, floating windows, slow drift, radius 0 or 0.25rem.

Wikipedia: mid-to-late 2000s, French house acts (College, Kavinsky); Outrun term from 1986 Out Run with VHS tracking artefacts, magenta neon, gridlines; Drive (2011). Does not name Sega.

note: Second independent source (Wikipedia) supports origin and motifs; examples list is empty, which is allowed. Radius ranges (and motion recipes) cited to daisyUI are that site's theme-token suggestions, not documented traits of the style; label them as a recommendation.

sources.note: daisyUI: Bethke and Gibson origins, palette, clipped panels, brackets, segmented bars, cable paths, condensed sans plus mono, scanlines, RGB split, flicker, high density, radius 0 or 0.25rem. Mentions Blade Runner only in a caption and not Syd Mead (origin rests on S2).

fixes.problem: Example says the HUD has cable-line decoration; the critique places the ribbon-cable lines on the Character (skill tree) screen, not the HUD. Red is decorative; yellow marks key info in the hacking interface.

note: Sound entry with two independent sources besides daisyUI; one small example wording fix. Radius ranges (and motion recipes) cited to daisyUI are that site's theme-token suggestions, not documented traits of the style; label them as a recommendation.

daisyUI: palette, motifs, playful display type, bobbing and ripple motion with bubbles, loose collage over wave bands, radius 0.75-1.5rem.

sources.note: daisyUI: mid-2000s to early-2010s commercial vector art; says the Frutiger Metro label was coined online in 2023 and is historically misleading; palette, motifs, type, radius.
pi.fyi user post by @jerb (2026), a personal opinion piece: about 2006-2010, black vectors over bright striated backgrounds, iPod ads, Xbox 360 home screens. Says nothing about who named it or when.

fixes.problem: The 2023 coinage date appears only on the daisyUI page; searches found no other source dating the label.
fixes.correct: Commercial vector art of the mid-2000s; the Frutiger Metro label is a later internet coinage of uncertain date [inferred]

fixes.problem: States the name has no link to Windows Metro, but Wikipedia (citing Avci) defines Frutiger Metro as a transitional style named after the Windows 8 Metro design language. The label has two competing meanings.
fixes.correct: Say the name is contested: some use it for vector silhouettes on bright stripes (Vectordelia), others for a flat transitional style named after Windows 8 Metro

fixes.problem: Date range 2006-2010 does not fit the main example: Apple's iPod silhouette campaign began in 2003 and ran to at least 2008.
fixes.correct: About 2003 to 2010, from the iPod silhouette ads onward

fixes.problem: Both sources are weak (a design-system trend page and a personal social post); no editorial or academic source names the style.
fixes.correct: Lead with the name Vectordelia, keep Frutiger Metro as a contested alias, keep confidence low, and add the iPod campaign as documented evidence of the look

note: Style is real but thinly sourced and its name is disputed; only the fan-level pi.fyi post independently supports the daisyUI description. sources.note: Wallpaper: Brent David Freaney of Special Offer Inc., 500 greens tested, Pantone 3507C, title in low-resolution Arial, plainness as the point.
The Nightly: hex #8ACE00, Arial with a horizontal stretch, 'opinionless' size, 100x100 px at 72 dpi scaled up, about 500 greens.
ACMI: July 2024 Kamala remix with lime overlay and fuzzy font; Harris team turned Kamala HQ on X lime green with the pixelated font.
NBC (24 Aug 2024): brat expressed through bright green and Arial, Etsy/eBay/Depop/Amazon copycat products, cafe drink. Arial mention is via one seller; no hex or Pantone.

fixes.problem: The style is one album's visual identity, and the entry states its exact brand colour (Pantone 3507C, #8ACE00) while the code uses #9ad600, a near-identical lime. That conflicts with OpenDesigner's rule against using an exact brand hue or a brand's identity.
fixes.correct: Describe it as one flat, garish acid colour with a single low-resolution lowercase word; keep the Pantone and hex only as a cited fact marked 'do not reuse', and set the code to a clearly different acid colour the user picks

fixes.problem: Arial is a proprietary Monotype face; the code already falls back to Arimo, which is fine, but defining calls for an 'Arial-style' look tied to the album.
fixes.correct: Name any plain neo-grotesque (open-licence) and keep Arial out of the recommendation

note: Facts all check out (Freaney, 500 greens, Pantone 3507C, 100 px blur, Kamala HQ); the problem is that it presents a single artist's identity and exact colour as the style.
